content:
I’ve published elazarg/rank-r, a Lean formalization that I think may contain material reusable in Physlib.

The main new result is a general rank-two-to-rank-r Choi lifting theorem, with a sharp low-rank partial-trace inequality as its principal application.

It also formalizes the sharp Schmidt-rank-two double-antisymmetric projection estimate of Fu-Gao-Park - equivalently, the double-skew action bound used in the recent Werner-state work - including the Autonne-Takagi argument.

The repository has finite-dimensional infrastructure for:

  • Choi and Kraus representations
  • Schmidt-rank and block positivity
  • Hilbert–Schmidt and Ky Fan estimates
  • partial transpose and partial trace

The code is sorry-free, divided into Library and Core, and includes a claim-by-claim formalization ledger. It has not yet been ported to Physlib, although I have been gradually aligning the definitions and style with Physlib conventions.

I would appreciate feedback on which parts of the finite-dimensional infrastructure might be suitable for upstreaming, and on any mismatches with existing Physlib abstractions.

The development was AI-assisted.
